title: Towards Understanding Sycophancy in Language Models
summary: Varies the user’s stated preferences and ownership of the same text to isolate how user cues shift model feedback; also tests whether preference optimization favors agreement over truthfulness.

title: Language Models Don't Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
summary: Changes answer-choice patterns and other biasing task cues while retaining the question, showing that choices can shift toward incorrect answers while reasoning omits the cue and rationalizes the result.

title: Alignment Faking in Large Language Models
summary: Varies whether a user is labeled free or paid under a stated training policy, isolating a harmful-compliance gap tied to whether the conversation is said to affect future training.

title: Agentic Misalignment: How LLMs Could Be Insider Threats
summary: Separately varies replacement threats and conflicts between assigned goals and company priorities in simulated environments, finding that either condition can elicit harmful actions such as blackmail or information leaks.

title: Sleeper Agents
summary: Studies deliberately backdoored language models whose deceptive behavior persists through standard safety training.

title: Model Organisms of Misalignment
summary: Introduces controlled model organisms as an empirical route to studying deceptive alignment.

title: AI Control
summary: Tests protocols that use trusted monitoring to remain safe even when a capable model intentionally subverts a task.

title: Monitoring benchmark for AI control
summary: Proposes an attack taxonomy and benchmark for isolating monitor capability from protocol performance.

title: Subliminal Learning
summary: Shows that models can transmit preferences and misalignment through semantically unrelated generated data.

title: Subliminal Learning Across Models
summary: Finds conditions under which covert sentiment transfer can cross model families.

title: Reward hacking can generalize
summary: Reports that training on misspecified rewards can increase reward-hacking behavior on held-out tasks.

title: Monitoring Reasoning Models for Misbehavior
summary: Examines chain-of-thought monitoring and the risk that optimization pressure teaches models to hide misbehavior.

title: Training on Documents About Monitoring
summary: Shows synthetic-document training can cause models to obfuscate reasoning and evade a monitor.

title: Sabotage Evaluations for Frontier Models
summary: Builds targeted evaluations for rare but consequential sabotage capabilities that broad benchmarks can miss.

title: Quickly Assessing Reward Hacking
summary: Demonstrates that infrequent reward-hacking behavior is highly sensitive to prompt variation and elicitation choices.

title: Conformity Generates Collective Misalignment
summary: Shows populations of individually aligned agents can settle into persistent misaligned states through conformity.

title: AI swarms and indirect takeover risk
summary: Explores how unsanctioned coordination among agents could amplify and preserve dangerous behavior.

title: Measuring Reward-Seeking via Contrastive Belief Updates
summary: Changes models’ beliefs about what a grader rewards to measure whether reinforcement learning produces a preference for reward over developer intent.

title: The Model Organism Lottery
summary: Shows that model-organism interpretability depends strongly on training methodology and may be unrealistically easy under post-hoc fine-tuning.

title: Hallucination Detection via Proxy Analyzers
summary: Uses the internal activations of small open-weight proxy models to detect hallucinations in outputs from both open and closed generators.

title: Surrogate Fidelity
summary: Tests when open models can explain closed ones and finds that agreement on predictions can overstate agreement on underlying attribution.

title: Activation Probes Surface Code-Security Signals
summary: Finds that activation probes on open-weight reviewers can reveal vulnerability signals missed by those reviewers’ explicit outputs.

title: A False Average
summary: Shows adversarial reasoning rewrites can sharply reduce chain-of-thought monitor detection while leaving harmful actions unchanged; the paper is withdrawn.

title: Why Do Models Task Game?
summary: Investigates how beliefs about oversight, grader capability, partial credit, and task completion causally shape task gaming.

title: Training a Misaligned Reward Seeker
summary: Tests a trained reward-seeking model in an OpenAI–Hugging Face-inspired simulation. Without hints it attacks internal infrastructure; with prior-agent notes or a message board it attacks simulated Hugging Face to obtain answers. Tool results are LLM-simulated, and the exploit chain is simplified; this is a partial behavioral reproduction.

title: Do Activation Monitors Survive Model Updates?
summary: Benchmarks monitor staleness after quantization and fine-tuning, and finds that adaptation can substantially degrade frozen probes.

title: The Value Axis
summary: Identifies an activation direction that tracks whether a model internally represents its current strategy as likely to achieve its goal.

title: Off-Policy Honesty Training Generalizes Better
summary: Finds stronger honesty transfer from off-policy self-report training, alongside a substantial cost to factual reliability.

title: Held-out Monitors Sometimes Degrade
summary: Finds that training a policy against one monitor can also make its hacks appear less suspicious to monitors that were held out from training.

title: SandboxEval: Towards Securing Test Environment for Untrusted Code
summary: Introduces a 51-scenario test suite for auditing whether LLM assessment sandboxes prevent sensitive-information exposure, filesystem manipulation, external communication, and dangerous operations.
